text: Changes in the degree of closeness. <break time="0.8s" /> Are quite important. <break time="0.8s" /> In managing emotional intensity. <break time="0.8s" /> Take, for example. <break time="0.8s" /> Emotions induced by television. <break time="0.8s" /> Closeness and familiarity are important. <break time="0.8s" /> In making the fictional environment more real. <break time="0.8s" /> Accordingly most TV shows are set in the present. <break time="0.8s" /> Or in a time within the memory of the viewers. <break time="0.8s" /> Most characters are supposed to be types with whom we are familiar. <break time="0.8s" /> Such closeness and familiarity make it easier. <break time="0.8s" /> For us to perceive the imaginary story. <break time="0.8s" /> To be a real one. <break time="0.8s" /> In other circumstances. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as when violence is shown on TV. <break time="0.8s" /> The closeness variable is used. <break time="0.8s" /> To reduce emotional intensity. <break time="0.8s" /> Television entertainment tends to place. <break time="0.8s" /> Social problems involving violence. <break time="0.8s" /> In another time and place. <break time="0.8s" /> Letting us watch those fictionalized characters. <break time="0.8s" /> Search for solutions to our problems. <break time="0.8s" /> In settings safely distanced from our own. <break time="0.8s" /> When violence occurs in a contemporary setting. <break time="0.8s" /> It is generally the product of the interaction of police and criminals. <break time="0.8s" /> Again it is removed from the lives of good citizenry.
